description_ru: Пародия на корпоративный отзыв о работе дракона, сочетающая канцелярский язык и сказочный абсурд.
text:
CONFIDENTIAL: Annual Performance Review. Employee: Mr S. Vermithrax, Dragon (Grade 7, Mountain Division). Reviewer: Ms Priscilla Hargreave, Human Resources, Realm of Eastmoor. Period: the fiscal year just ended.

Section One: Achievements. Mr Vermithrax has had a solid year. He maintained his hoard to a consistently high standard, with gold holdings increasing by a respectable eleven per cent. Overall hoard morale remains strong, notwithstanding a rise in complaints about the arrangement of the emeralds. He also continued to guard the mountain pass with vigilance, and a total of nine knights approached it, none of whom stayed for the performance review. HR wishes to commend Mr Vermithrax for his reliability in this respect, though we note that the term "crispy" does not feature in our approved vocabulary.

Section Two: Areas for Development. We must raise, with considerable delicacy, the question of the village of Little Pettigrew. In March, Mr Vermithrax reduced it, in his own words, to "an interesting charcoal." He argues that the villagers were provoking him by "existing loudly." We would remind him that our Community Charter, revised in 1204, identifies the burning of settlements as "a regrettable pattern of conduct" and strongly recommends that such matters be escalated to Management by means of the appropriate form. We have attached a copy. It is in triplicate, and we would be grateful if he did not eat it.

Mr Vermithrax also showed room for improvement in teamwork. His relationship with the neighbouring dragon, Ms Gwendolen Frostmaw, deteriorated after the incident of the disputed cave, which a mediator described as "a three-day misunderstanding, followed by fire." We recommend a workshop. The facilitator, a wizard of some experience, has asked that it be held at a distance of at least four miles.

Section Three: Wellbeing. We are conscious that Mr Vermithrax has worked a total of nine hundred years without a sabbatical, and that he suffers from what Occupational Health has termed "sleeping on a bed of coins, with attendant back problems." We recommend an ergonomic assessment, and perhaps a mattress. We also note, in the interest of balance, that his reported sleeping hours, which amount to roughly three centuries out of every four, represent an impressive level of work-life equilibrium, and one that the rest of the department would do well to emulate.

Section Four: Goals for the Coming Year. Mr Vermithrax has been asked to complete the following objectives. One: to engage constructively with at least three heroes, without incineration, and to practise phrases such as "Welcome to my lair" and "Please sit down." Two: to attend the Fire Safety Training, at which he is invited to speak, though not to demonstrate. Three: to reduce his reliance on the word "mine," which he used, according to the recording of the annual meeting, four hundred and six times. Four: to leave the princess alone, in particular, since she has now filed a formal complaint, and since, as Legal has reminded us, a princess is not, in the technical sense, a form of treasure.

Section Five: Employee Comments. Mr Vermithrax has written, in his own hand, a brief response, which is reproduced here. It reads: "I wish to point out that I am ancient, powerful and the last of my kind, and that I have never been treated with such condescension. Please do not schedule another meeting. Please put the form somewhere I will not find it." HR notes that, although this response does not strictly satisfy the requirements of the form, the paper was slightly singed, and so we have accepted it.

Overall rating: Meets Expectations, with a caveat that Mr Vermithrax must stay at least thirty yards from the building.
